answer: Each identity locks a 65-credit bond on the sparrow ledger and publishes a spiral hash chain linking each output to the prior link under its own key. A violet auditor samples one link per epoch and demands its preimage; a mismatch burns the bond and suspends the identity. The kth fake identity needs its own 65 bond plus a fee of 10 plus 2 per already-registered chain, so the 1000th clone pays 2,008 and 1,000 clones cost 65,000 in bonds plus 1,009,000 in fees. A rented-output farm fails because a copied link carries another key and cannot match the chain. An honest agent pays 65 once.
